title: Encode String With Shortest Length
description:
Given a string s, encode the string such that its encoded length is the shortest.
The encoding rule is: k[encoded_string], where the encoded_string inside the square brackets is being repeated exactly k times. k should be a positive integer.
If an encoding process does not make the string shorter, then do not encode it. If there are several shortest encodings, return the lexicographically smallest one. Only use a repeated-block encoding when it is strictly shorter than the decoded substring. Return s unchanged if no encoding is shorter than s.

## Examples

### Example 1

```text
Input: s = "aaa"
Output: "aaa"
```

There is no way to encode it such that it is shorter than the input string, so we do not encode it.

### Example 2

```text
Input: s = "aaaaa"
Output: "5[a]"
```

"5[a]" is shorter than "aaaaa" by 1 character.

### Example 3

```text
Input: s = "aaaaaaaaaa"
Output: "10[a]"
```

"10[a]" is the lexicographically smallest shortest encoding.

## Constraints

- 1 <= s.length <= 150
- s consists of only lowercase English letters.
